summary: Verified the settings merge bug fix on /settings page. All three test scenarios PASSED: (1) Turning OFF 'Require PO for Purchase' with confirm dialog then turning OFF 'FEFO Consumption Tracking' — require_po stayed OFF (previously reverted to ON). (2) After page refresh, both toggles remained OFF confirming API persistence. (3) Reverse direction — turning both back ON also worked without either resetting the other. The read-merge-write pattern in updateOperationalSettings works correctly in both directions.
critical_code_review_comments: Read-merge-write pattern in api.js updateOperationalSettings is correct approach but has a race condition risk: if two toggles are clicked rapidly, both may read the same stored_settings snapshot and the second write can clobber the first. Consider adding a mutex/queue or moving the merge to the backend (PATCH semantics instead of full replace).
seed_data_creation: None. Used pre-existing manager@germanfluid.com account. Settings were toggled OFF then back ON during test, final state: both require_po_for_purchase and fefo_consumption_enabled = ON.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Settings merge bug is fixed. All toggle interactions preserve other settings correctly. Confirm dialog for high-impact toggles uses button:text-is('Disable') / 'Enable' — not scoped to [role='dialog'] container reliably; use plain text selector.
rca of the issue: Original bug: POS /api/operational-settings did a full replace of stored_settings dict. Frontend was sending only the single changed key which caused all other keys to be dropped on the server side. Fix (in api.js updateOperationalSettings): before POSTing, first GET the current stored_settings, merge in the changed key, then send the complete merged object. Verified via UI E2E test — the toggled-off require_po remained off after toggling fefo, and both persisted across page refresh.
